newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: U.S. investment in S.Africa growing despite crime.
newsitem.headline: U.S. investment in S.Africa growing despite crime.

text.p: U.S. investment in South Africa is growing at 25 percent a year, despite the country's widely-publicised crime problem, an American Chamber of Commerce official said on Wednesday.

"A crime survey by the American business community, which is due to be released soon, shows that crime still does not seem to be a deterrent to U.S. investment which is coming in and adapting to, and coming to terms with it," said Bill Mallory, the chamber's immediate past president.
"Trade between America and South Africa is growing at 25 percent per annum, and is expected to do so for some time," he added.
The American Chamber of Commerce opened an office in South Africa's KwaZulu-Natal province on Wednesday to facilitate easier trade and to access southern African markets.

"It is important that U.S. companies investing in South Africa have backup in the form of their own chamber of commerce to represent their interests in this part of the world," said Luanne Grant, director of the chamber in South Africa.
American interest in South Africa was growing very quickly and U.S. companies were eyeing the country as a springboard into the 12 member Southern African Development Community, said Mallory.

"There is tremendous growth potential in SADC (Southern Africa Development Community) and American companies are not specifically targeting South African markets but are seeing South Africa as a base to access the region's markets," he said.

He said some 42 U.S. companies were based in Durban, half of which were members of the chamber. The chamber in South Africa had 267 members, half of which were entirely U.S.-owned and 70 of which were in the Fortune 500 of top global concerns.
U.S. investment in South Africa since 1994 has totalled some 10 billion rand.
